title: Generic isomorphism open of a proper birational map
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover). Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper birational morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Birational means that $f$ maps the generic points of the irreducible components of $Y$ bijectively onto those of $X$ and induces isomorphisms $\mathcal O_{X,f(\eta)}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ at all these points [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then there is a dense open $V\subseteq X$ containing every generic point of every irreducible component of $X$, such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $f$ is separated and of finite type. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], it is therefore locally of finite type. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian by hypothesis, [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $f$ locally of finite presentation. No reducedness hypothesis is needed.

By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components], $X$ has finitely many irreducible components. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], components of either scheme correspond bijectively to their generic points: each has exactly one, and its closure recovers that component. The assumed bijection of component generic points consequently gives a bijection between the components of $Y$ and those of $X$. Thus $Y$ also has finitely many irreducible components.

source.place: Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components); Schemes Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); finite-component hypotheses in Morphisms 0BAJ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-birational-isomorphism-dense-open] to the given morphism $f$: separatedness and local finite presentation are Step 1, finiteness of the two component sets is Step 2, and the bijection and generic-local-ring isomorphisms are precisely the birationality hypotheses of the item. This yields a dense open $V\subseteq X$ such that the entire inverse-image restriction $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ (lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open), separated and locally-finite-presentation alternatives; Varieties 0BFP, proof (1).

proof.text: Fix an irreducible component $C$ of $X$ with generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components]. Write $C_1,\ldots,C_r$ for the other components and put $O=X\setminus\bigcup_jC_j$. Distinct components cannot contain $\xi$: being closed, they would then contain $\overline{\{\xi\}}=C$, contradicting maximality. Hence $O$ is open and contains $\xi$. Every point lies on a component by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], so $O\subseteq C$. Density of $V$ gives $z\in O\cap V$. Since $z\in C=\overline{\{\xi\}}$, the open neighbourhood $V$ of $z$ meets $\{\xi\}$; thus $\xi\in V$. This proves the additional generic-point clause. For $X=\varnothing$, the empty open is dense, Step 3 still applies, and the clause is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0052 (lemma-Noetherian), finite-component open-piece argument; Tag 004W (lemma-irreducible), part (4); elementary closure argument for Varieties 0BFP(1).
